purpose: CHPE project operation, heat-event use, outage and repair, and the still-open bridge to customer incidence, mitigation, and durable public legitimacy

events.geography: United States and Canada; Quebec to New York City Zone J
events.date_precision: Reported commercial-operation date; announcement published June 16, 2026
events.denominator: One named 339-mile cross-border transmission project; expected annual delivery is 10.4 TWh, not observed household receipt
events.method: Structured extraction from NYSERDA/New York State project announcement and Tier Four program materials
events.missingness: No hourly availability series, retail bill, rate-class allocation, customer receipt, route-community burden, compensation, or durable acceptance record
events.exposure: CHPE reached commercial operation and is reported as delivering Hydro-Québec power into the New York metropolitan area
events.alternatives_before_action: New York capacity, imports, and other generation or transmission resources are system alternatives; customer-level alternatives are not observed
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: A cross-border delivery route became operational with projected annual energy and emissions benefits; realized customer affordability and local burden are not measured
events.choice_or_response: The project entered commercial operation under the state Tier Four delivery framework; load-serving entities and customers have no linked receipt or choice record
events.person_or_actor_with_control: Project operator, Hydro-Québec, NYSERDA, NYISO, and New York load-serving entities control project delivery and market/accounting interfaces; affected customers and route communities are not linked
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: Commercial operation and the Tier Four delivery/accounting framework are documented; no event-specific customer remedy or community compensation is observed
events.immediate_outcome: Named cross-border infrastructure moved from construction and contract into reported commercial operation
events.protected_outcome: The project may provide clean-energy delivery and resource-adequacy value; household reliability or affordability protection is not established
events.sacrificed_outcome: Construction, contract, transmission, and route-community costs may be distributed across actors; incidence is not observed
events.cost_risk_transfer: The project creates a cross-border dependence and contractual delivery route, but the allocation of project cost, market value, and risk is not traceable to households
events.later_outcome: Later operation and an early outage are reported; customer bills, service continuity, mitigation, acceptance, and geopolitical leverage remain open
events.meaning_and_attribution: No linked customer or host-community fairness, attribution, trust, or legitimacy judgment is observed
events.public_or_collective_response: State and operator announcements are visible; affected-unit participation, contestation, and later collective response are not linked
events.counterexample: Commercial operation can be real while projected annual delivery and emissions figures remain different from realized household benefit or durable public acceptance
events.source_and_uncertainty: NYSERDA/New York State announcement and Tier Four materials; projected delivery and public effects are not customer-level observations

events.geography: United States; NYISO and New York City Zone J
events.date_precision: July 3-4, 2026 heat-event and early repair episode
events.denominator: One named CHPE operating episode within a NYISO heat event; Canadian imports include flows beyond CHPE
events.method: Structured extraction from EIA analysis using NYISO hourly data and official project context
events.missingness: No customer outage, retail bill, outage duration, repair cost, facility-level dispatch, or affected-unit remedy is retained
events.exposure: EIA reported 52 GWh of Canadian imports on July 3, 9% of NYISO demand, and full 1,250 MW CHPE utilization; CHPE was taken offline again July 4 for repairs after an earlier June outage
events.alternatives_before_action: Other generation, imports, demand response, and system operating resources could contribute during heat stress; their unit-level substitution is not isolated
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: The episode shows high operating use during heat stress alongside early availability friction; household service and price incidence are not measured
events.choice_or_response: The operator and system used CHPE during the heat event and removed it for repair; customer and host-place responses are not linked
events.person_or_actor_with_control: CHPE operator and NYISO controlled operating and repair decisions within system constraints; customers had no observed event-specific control record
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: Repair and continued system operation are reported; no customer compensation, replacement, or public contestation outcome is observed
events.immediate_outcome: The project supplied a visible operating contribution during heat stress, but operation was interrupted soon afterward
events.protected_outcome: CHPE may have contributed to system supply during the heat event; protection of any named customer or service is not established
events.sacrificed_outcome: Availability, repair resources, and potentially other system resources carried operating costs; their incidence is not observed
events.cost_risk_transfer: A project can support system supply while outage risk remains with operators, substitute resources, and customers; the transfer is not quantified
events.later_outcome: The outage-and-repair sequence creates a later availability test; sustained performance, affordability, and acceptance remain unknown
events.meaning_and_attribution: No linked affected-unit attribution, trust, fairness, or legitimacy response is observed
events.public_or_collective_response: Public operational reporting is visible; customer complaints, organizing, and later political response are not linked
events.counterexample: High utilization during heat stress does not prove durable reliability, and an early outage does not prove project failure or household harm
events.source_and_uncertainty: EIA analysis using NYISO hourly grid data and official project context; Canadian imports are broader than CHPE and customer incidence is absent

events.geography: United States and Canada; CHPE and New York City reliability-planning context
events.date_precision: August-September 2026 operator status and planning cross-read; exact status-post date is not retained
events.denominator: One named CHPE project and related planning case; not an independent post-repair availability denominator
events.method: Structured extraction from operator public status and public NYISO/utility reliability-planning context
events.missingness: No independent hourly availability, dispatch, delivered energy, customer bill, reliability protection, repair cost, compensation, or acceptance record
events.exposure: The operator describes CHPE as fully operational after commissioning, while planning materials continue to distinguish CHPE-in and CHPE-out resource-adequacy cases
events.alternatives_before_action: CHPE-in and CHPE-out planning cases represent system alternatives; customer-level replacement or non-use is not observed
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: Restored operator status and planning relevance are visible; sustained availability and customer benefit are not independently measured
events.choice_or_response: The operator reports restored operation and planners retain CHPE as a reliability input; no affected customer or community response is linked
events.person_or_actor_with_control: Operator and system planners control status and planning treatment; customers, route communities, and public participants have no linked outcome record
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: Repair recovery and reliability-planning treatment are documented; no household or host-place remedy is observed
events.immediate_outcome: A post-repair recovery claim is visible while independent performance verification remains open
events.protected_outcome: Planning treatment may preserve system resource-adequacy options; realized reliability or affordability protection is not established
events.sacrificed_outcome: Dependence on a cross-border project may leave system and customers exposed to future availability or repair risk; no realized incidence is observed
events.cost_risk_transfer: The project remains a state and market dependency, but the distribution of outage, contract, and replacement risk is unresolved
events.later_outcome: Sustained operation, customer receipt, mitigation, acceptance, reversal, and external dependence response remain open
events.meaning_and_attribution: Operator recovery language is not a linked public legitimacy or customer-trust measure
events.public_or_collective_response: No event-specific later public response, contestation, or external-state reaction is linked
events.counterexample: A fully-operational operator statement can coexist with short interruptions, capacity constraints, or conservative planning assumptions
events.source_and_uncertainty: Operator public status cross-read with public reliability-planning context; neither supplies independent customer-level outcome evidence

events.geography: United States; CHPE and NYISO Zone J
events.date_precision: First-summer analysis published September 29, 2026; operating window June-September 2026
events.denominator: One named CHPE project; five-minute operating intervals and hot-day Zone J price observations in a secondary market analysis
events.method: Structured extraction from Modo Energy first-summer analysis; secondary market-data interpretation, not an independent household-bill evaluation
events.missingness: No retail bill, rate-class allocation, customer receipt, outage-service effect, repair cost, compensation, or route-community acceptance is retained
events.exposure: The analysis reports zero output in 83% of five-minute intervals during June-August, average running output of 940 MW against a 1,250 MW rating, a 13% first-summer capacity factor, and a cable fault that removed 20 full operational days from July 4
events.alternatives_before_action: Zone J generation, storage, imports, and other system resources could substitute during non-operation; the analysis does not identify customer-level substitution or cost
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: On 85-90F days, the analysis reports a $17/MW-day Zone J day-ahead four-hour spread premium when CHPE ran versus $85/MW-day when it did not; real-time premiums did not show the same compression
events.choice_or_response: CHPE operated as an afternoon-to-evening block after repair and was offline during the cable-fault period; customer and host-place responses are not linked
events.person_or_actor_with_control: CHPE operator and NYISO controlled operation within system constraints; households, rate classes, and route communities are not linked
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: Repair and subsequent operating pattern are reported; no customer compensation, replacement, or bill-level remedy is observed
events.immediate_outcome: The first-summer record adds an observed availability and conditional wholesale-price mechanism to the commercial-operation sequence
events.protected_outcome: The project may reduce a day-ahead Zone J spread during selected hot-day operating periods; household affordability and reliability protection are not established
events.sacrificed_outcome: Forced-outage exposure, intermittent availability, and substitute-resource costs remain possible; their incidence is not measured
events.cost_risk_transfer: The operating profile makes project availability and system-dependence risk visible without showing who bears it or whether any price effect reaches customers
events.later_outcome: Post-repair operating continuity, customer incidence, mitigation, acceptance, and external dependence response remain open
events.meaning_and_attribution: No linked customer or host-community fairness, trust, attribution, or legitimacy measure is observed
events.public_or_collective_response: Secondary market analysis is public; customer complaints, organizing, and later political response are not linked
events.counterexample: A conditional day-ahead spread difference can reflect operating selection and does not establish causal retail-price savings; a 13% capacity factor does not alone prove project failure
events.source_and_uncertainty: Modo Energy analysis using five-minute operating and market data; the source is secondary, its counterfactual construction is not independently reproduced here, and the result does not establish household incidence

events.geography: United States; NYSERDA Tier 4 program and NYISO Zone J
events.date_precision: Commercial-operation date stated on the current NYSERDA Tier 4 program page
events.denominator: One Tier 4 program contract and its CHPE delivery-accounting rule; not a household or retail-bill denominator
events.method: Structured extraction from NYSERDA's official Tier 4 program page
events.missingness: No individual REC retirement, load-serving-entity bill, household credit, retail price, or customer-level use is retained
events.exposure: NYSERDA states that Tier 4 RECs are procured only after qualified renewable energy is verified as generated, scheduled, and delivered into NYISO Zone J on an hourly basis
events.alternatives_before_action: Other clean-energy attributes, contracts, and generation resources may satisfy separate policy obligations; customer-level alternatives are not observed
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: The rule creates a verifiable delivery-to-REC accounting condition and a ratepayer-protection mechanism; it does not report a household bill effect
events.choice_or_response: NYSERDA administers the REC contract and hourly matching rule; load-serving entities and REC buyers operate within the program, without linked household choice records
events.person_or_actor_with_control: NYSERDA and the program contract control attribute eligibility and accounting; NYISO verifies delivery context; households are not linked to the transaction
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: Hourly matching is an institutional control against crediting undelivered energy, not a customer remedy or compensation event
events.immediate_outcome: The program connects CHPE operation to an explicit hourly verification and REC-accounting stage
events.protected_outcome: The rule may protect program integrity and ratepayers from paying for unverified attributes; realized household protection is not measured
events.sacrificed_outcome: Administrative, contract, and market participation costs may be incurred; their distribution is not observed
events.cost_risk_transfer: The accounting rule shifts verification responsibility into the program and market interface, but does not identify who ultimately bears costs or receives savings
events.later_outcome: A later REC sale and avoided-ratepayer-cost claim are documented; household receipt, adequacy, trust, and acceptance remain open
events.meaning_and_attribution: Program accountability is visible; no linked household or host-community attribution or legitimacy judgment is observed
events.public_or_collective_response: The public program rule is documented; affected-unit participation and later collective response are not linked
events.counterexample: Hourly matching can improve attribute-accounting integrity without showing that a particular household received lower-cost or more reliable electricity
events.source_and_uncertainty: Official NYSERDA Tier 4 page; the matching rule is program-level and does not establish retail-bill incidence

events.geography: United States; NYSERDA Tier 4 voluntary REC market
events.date_precision: 2027 vintage voluntary summer sale closed September 2, 2026; invoices due October 3, 2026
events.denominator: One NYSERDA voluntary Tier 4 REC sale: 50,000 offered and 16,376 sold; not a household or ratepayer receipt denominator
events.method: Structured extraction from NYSERDA's official 2027 voluntary-sales page
events.missingness: No individual customer credit, retail bill, REC retirement, buyer pass-through, household benefit, or local acceptance record is retained
events.exposure: NYSERDA reports 16,376 CHPE-sourced Tier 4 RECs sold at $35.52 each, $581,675.52 in presale revenue, and approximately $582,000 in avoided ratepayer costs; buyers included commercial real estate and other purchasers
events.alternatives_before_action: Buyers could decline or choose other environmental attributes; ratepayer and household alternatives are not observed
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: The sale creates a reported program-level revenue and avoided-cost mechanism; it does not show which households saw a bill change or how costs were distributed
events.choice_or_response: NYSERDA offered and sold the RECs; buyer participation and invoice administration are reported, while customer use and pass-through remain unobserved
events.person_or_actor_with_control: NYSERDA controls the sale and contract administration; REC buyers control purchases; households and load-serving entities have no linked individual transaction record
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: The avoided-ratepayer-cost claim is a program-level financial outcome, not a verified household remedy or receipt
events.immediate_outcome: CHPE-linked environmental attributes moved through a dated sale with a quantified program-level financial result
events.protected_outcome: The sale may reduce program costs charged to ratepayers according to NYSERDA's summary; household-level protection is not independently observed
events.sacrificed_outcome: The sale price, administrative costs, and attribute value may be distributed unevenly among buyers, the program, and ratepayers; incidence is unresolved
events.cost_risk_transfer: The transaction creates a possible transfer from REC buyers and program revenue to ratepayer-cost avoidance, but no customer-level allocation is available
events.later_outcome: Invoice due date and retirement deadline are stated; completed payment, retirement, bill posting, household adequacy, and durable acceptance remain open
events.meaning_and_attribution: The sale makes a public-benefit accounting claim visible; no linked ratepayer trust or fairness response is observed
events.public_or_collective_response: Buyer demographics are summarized; public participation, contestation, and later political response are not linked
events.counterexample: Avoided ratepayer costs reported at the program level cannot be converted into an equal household credit or a realized retail-price reduction
events.source_and_uncertainty: Official NYSERDA sale summary; revenue and avoided-cost figures are program-level reported results and do not establish household pass-through

events.geography: United States; New York Control Area and NYISO market operations
events.date_precision: NYISO daily capacity report dated October 1, 2026
events.denominator: One NYISO capacity-report snapshot; CHPE import schedule is 1,250 MW and NYCA capacity margin is 446 MW in the report
events.method: Structured extraction from NYISO's public daily capacity report
events.missingness: No retail customer, bill, reliability interruption avoided, facility-level payment, or household/service incidence is retained
events.exposure: NYISO's report lists a 1,250 MW CHPE import schedule and a 1,250 MW import limit alongside the day's NYCA capacity summary
events.alternatives_before_action: The same report lists other interconnections and in-state capacity; their substitution for CHPE at the customer level is not observed
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: The snapshot independently confirms a scheduled operating import and system-capacity role; it does not measure a household benefit
events.choice_or_response: NYISO scheduled and reported the CHPE import within daily capacity operations; no affected customer choice or service response is linked
events.person_or_actor_with_control: NYISO controls market scheduling and reporting; generators, importers, and load-serving entities operate within the system; households are not linked
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: Daily capacity reporting supplies an operational accountability record, not a customer remedy
events.immediate_outcome: CHPE appears as a named, fully scheduled 1,250 MW import in an independent NYISO operating snapshot
events.protected_outcome: The scheduled import may contribute to the reported NYCA capacity margin; avoided outage or customer reliability is not established
events.sacrificed_outcome: Import dependence and associated market or contractual costs remain possible; their incidence is not measured
events.cost_risk_transfer: The report makes system dependence visible but does not identify who pays for, benefits from, or bears the risk of the import
events.later_outcome: The snapshot supports an operating-stage sequence; sustained reliability, affordability, customer receipt, and acceptance remain open
events.meaning_and_attribution: Operational scheduling is visible; no linked customer attribution, fairness, trust, or legitimacy judgment is observed
events.public_or_collective_response: NYISO's public report is available; event-specific public response and external-state reaction are not linked
events.counterexample: A scheduled import can coexist with later outage, congestion, price, or customer-service problems
events.source_and_uncertainty: Official NYISO daily capacity report; a single snapshot cannot establish sustained availability, causality, or household incidence

arrows.evidence: The named project has both a commercial-operation milestone and a dated heat-event utilization/outage record.
arrows.counterexample: The same project-level sequence does not establish a customer-level service effect or causal reliability benefit.
arrows.remaining_gap: Hourly availability, causal customer effect, outage duration, and project-level replacement are not linked.

arrows.to: first-summer availability profile and conditional day-ahead spread difference
arrows.evidence: Modo Energy reports a 20-day cable-fault outage, 13% first-summer capacity factor, zero output in 83% of June-August five-minute intervals, and a lower Zone J day-ahead spread premium on selected hot days when CHPE ran.
arrows.counterexample: The secondary analysis does not establish a causal retail-price effect, and intermittent operation does not alone establish project failure or household harm.
arrows.remaining_gap: Independent time-series reproduction, customer-class allocation, retail bill effect, avoided service loss, repair cost, and host-place response are not linked.

arrows.evidence: The outage-and-repair episode is followed by an operator-reported fully-operational status and continued planning treatment.
arrows.counterexample: Operator recovery status can coexist with short interruptions or capacity constraints not visible in the public status statement.
arrows.remaining_gap: Independent post-repair performance, delivered energy, customer service, and durable reliability are not observed.

arrows.evidence: The project is treated as an operating and planning resource after commercial operation.
arrows.counterexample: Planning treatment is a formal resource assumption, not a realized price, bill, or reliability outcome.
arrows.remaining_gap: Planning relevance is not proof of realized bill, reliability, local, or geopolitical benefit.

arrows.evidence: The retained project and operating records identify the project and system context.
arrows.counterexample: A system operating record may have no compatible customer-level measure even when the project is genuinely operating.
arrows.remaining_gap: No compatible customer class, bill, service, outage, or affordability observation is joined to the project.

arrows.evidence: The planning record distinguishes CHPE-in and CHPE-out cases.
arrows.counterexample: A planning alternative is not an observed customer replacement, compensation, or usable non-use option.
arrows.remaining_gap: No observed customer or system replacement, compensation, or usable alternative is tied to the outage or future non-use.

arrows.evidence: The project is a named cross-border dependency with public operator and state-planning records.
arrows.counterexample: Cross-border project status does not itself establish public acceptance or changed external-state behavior.
arrows.remaining_gap: No linked host-community acceptance, public contestation, customer trust, or changed external-state behavior is observed.

arrows.to: hourly delivery verification and REC eligibility
arrows.evidence: NYSERDA states that CHPE-linked Tier 4 RECs require hourly generation, scheduling, and delivery verification into NYISO Zone J.
arrows.counterexample: Verification establishes attribute-accounting eligibility, not household affordability or reliability benefit.
arrows.remaining_gap: No customer-class allocation, bill, or individual REC-to-household link is observed.

arrows.from: hourly delivery verification and REC eligibility
arrows.to: dated REC sale and reported avoided ratepayer cost
arrows.evidence: NYSERDA reports a 2027 voluntary sale of 16,376 CHPE-sourced Tier 4 RECs for $581,675.52 and approximately $582,000 in avoided ratepayer costs.
arrows.counterexample: A program-level avoided-cost result is not a verified household credit or equal retail-price reduction.
arrows.remaining_gap: Completed payment, retirement, pass-through, and customer-level receipt are not retained.

arrows.evidence: The official sale page names avoided ratepayer costs as a program result.
arrows.counterexample: Avoided program cost can coexist with unchanged or heterogeneous household bills.
arrows.remaining_gap: No compatible ratepayer denominator, bill posting, household credit, or service outcome is observed.

arrows.evidence: The transaction makes a cross-border public-benefit and ratepayer-protection claim visible.
arrows.counterexample: A quantified program benefit does not establish trust, consent, or changed Canada–U.S. behavior.
arrows.remaining_gap: No linked public legitimacy, contestation, household attribution, or external-state response is observed.

arrows.evidence: NYISO's October 1, 2026 capacity report lists a 1,250 MW CHPE import schedule and a matching 1,250 MW import limit.
arrows.counterexample: A daily schedule confirms an operating record for that snapshot but does not establish continuous availability or customer benefit.
arrows.remaining_gap: No sustained series, customer-class allocation, bill, or avoided-service-loss measure is linked.
